headline: MGAT Alpha closed 13 trades this week for +$114.02 (53.85% win rate) against a paper book, a clear turnaround from last week's 0-for-6. One family (BC) carried almost all of the gain (6 of 7 closes, +$107.54) while L1 posted a clean sweep of small time-stop losses and DEX's single close was a small loss. Measured-beta coverage held steady at 69.23% of new positions. Two open data-quality questions -- one trade whose exit price sits far off its independent check, and an unexplained gap in the counterfactual ledger's history -- keep this week's numbers provisional rather than final, and the sample (19 of a 200-trade target) is still far too small to call the logic healthy or broken.
llm_adviser: No restart events this week -- the run has not rebooted since launch, and both boot records still read llm_mode: 'active'. It remains UNCONFIRMED whether this reflects the intended adviser switch (agreed state: OFF) or an unrelated runtime flag; unverified against source, so treat it as an open question rather than a settled OFF.
sample_caveat: 13 closed trades this week, 19 all-time against the 200-trade target -- roughly 9.5% of the way to a sample size worth treating as meaningful. Win rate (53.85% week, 36.84% all-time) and PnL% are still not a fully reliable read at this size: a couple of trades reversing outcome would move the all-time win rate several points, and the one flagged trade below already accounts for a meaningful share of this week's apparent gain.
paper_caveat: Alpha is paper -- simulated fills, no slippage, no thin-liquidity exits, no can't-sell-into-dust. A clean logic result here is never a claim that the execution floor works; that claim belongs to the Beta rung alone.
integrity: No CLASS-A changes landed this week -- clean comparison. A separate data-integrity question about the counterfactual ledger's own history remains open (see verdict) and is unresolved, but it is not a repair-log item.

verdict.text: Taken at face value this week is a clear turnaround from launch week: 7 wins of 13 closes (53.85%) versus 0-for-6, +$114.02 versus -$86.98, with BC carrying the book (6-for-7) while L1's three closes were ordinary time-stop losses and DEX's one close was a small loss -- nothing here reads as broken trading logic, and the regime was calm (146 of 168 cycles neutral, no critical alarms). But two open questions sit directly on top of the numbers. One BC close is flagged more than 1,000% off its independent check price and is currently the largest single contributor to this week's realized gain; until that price is verified, the win rate and PnL should be read as provisional. Separately, the counterfactual ledger's history now starts partway through the week with no positions predating it, at odds with the prior week's stated count, with no recorded change that explains it. Neither is a fault in the trading sense, but both are data-quality gaps large enough to resolve before trusting the headline numbers outright, and the sample is still small (19 of 200) even setting the two flags aside.
